review.tagline: Python library and CLI for face detection, landmarks and matching, built on dlib
review.summary: Python library built on dlib that finds faces in images, returns landmarks for eyes, nose, mouth and chin, and compares face encodings to identify people. It also installs `face_recognition` and `face_detection` CLI tools that process folders of images, with a `--tolerance` setting (default 0.6) and `--cpus` for parallel runs. The README cites 99.38% accuracy on Labeled Faces in the Wild.
review.audience: Python developers adding face detection or matching to scripts and apps
strengths: Few-line Python API: face_locations, face_landmarks, face_encodings, compare_faces
CLI tools identify faces across image folders, with --cpus for multi-core runs
Many runnable examples: webcam, video file, Raspberry Pi, Flask service, KNN and SVM
Optional CNN detector with GPU batch support when dlib is built with CUDA
weaknesses: Last release is 2018-04-02, so PyPI lags the repository
Requires building dlib with cmake; Windows is not officially supported
README says accuracy is weaker on children and varies between ethnic groups
CNN detection model needs a GPU for good performance
needs: Needs dlib, cmake, Python 3.3+ or 2.7, OpenCV (webcam/video examples), Flask (web service example)
Models: dlib HOG face detector, dlib CNN face detector, dlib ResNet face encodings
